bottleneck: Delivering editors to oocytes, spermatogonia, or early embryos for research faces the same mosaicism and off-target problems as somatic editing, compounded by the impossibility of validating safety in the resulting child before birth. Animal models do not fully predict human developmental responses to editing, and human embryo research is restricted to the first 14 days in most jurisdictions — before most developmental consequences manifest.
current_state: Basic research continues under the 14-day rule and national bans. The validation gap between embryo models and a safe live birth is unbridgeable with current tools.

title: Embryo editing safety cannot be validated pre-birth
why_it_blocks: The first child of embryo editing would be the experiment. This unresolvable validation paradox is why clinical germline editing remains both technically premature and ethically out of reach.
